We can have one of 2 options after leaving the first seat n professors: 1) The last passenger will sit in the first seat, or 2) The last passenger will sit in the last seat. In case 1, everyone will occupy their existing seats, and in case 2, everyone will still occupy their existing seats.

Therefore, we can write the recurrence relation: pi(n) = 0.5 x pi(n - 1) + 0.5. This recurrence relation appears to represent priority ordering between the last two passengers, where the first passenger distinguishes their position by a fair coin flip. But because after leaving the first seat, there are no longer any places after the second seat to seat anyone, each passenger has the same chance of sitting in the next seat. Therefore, the final probability distribution is uniform over all n seats.
